stem.en: How do chloroplasts and chromoplasts differ in their pigments?

text.en: Both hold only chlorophyll, in different amounts.

feedback.en: Chromoplasts hold pigments other than chlorophyll.

text.en: Chloroplasts hold no pigment, and chromoplasts hold chlorophyll.

feedback.en: This has the two the wrong way round.

text.en: Chloroplasts hold green chlorophyll; chromoplasts hold yellow, orange or red.

feedback.en: Yes. That difference gives leaves and fruits their different colours.

text.en: Chloroplasts are white, and chromoplasts have no pigment of any colour at all.

explanation.en: Chloroplasts hold the green pigment chlorophyll. Chromoplasts hold yellow, orange or red pigments.

hints.en: What does the Greek word chroma mean?
